result.title: Building heterogeneous multistep workflows in automated microscopy: reward design and knowledge transfer for autonomous structure property discovery
result.summary: Autonomous microscopy can turn fast acquisition into scientific progress when it decides not only where to measure, but also what information to acquire, at what scan rate, and when to recalibrate the instrument. We develop a budget constrained framework for such multistep structure-property workflows. It combines explicit scientific rewards, action costs, instrument observation models, transfer of pre experiment knowledge into the online campaign, and evaluation kept independent of the controller. The transferred knowledge includes predictor accuracy and computational cost, empirical learner maturity functions that weight model-derived rewards, and drift characteristics established before controller training. Using a real electron energy-loss spectroscopy dataset, we run two complementary campaigns. In the first, the controller chooses between imaging and spectroscopy, image size, and scan speed. In the second, the instrument drifts and the controller also decides when to recalibrate. The campaigns show that response discovery and structure-property learning favor different surrogate models and acquisition strategies. They also show that simple acquisition rules form strong, practical baselines. Independent error analysis reveals where model uncertainty is and is not a reliable learning signal. In the drift campaign, explicit registration greatly improves positional accuracy, and the framework measures what this costs in spectroscopy throughput. Together, these results provide a reproducible way to design, compare, and audit autonomous experiments, and they define what microscopes must provide for deployment: independently executable actions, characterized scan and detector responses, timestamped registration telemetry, and complete action records.

AI.brief_summary: 提出预算约束的多步自主显微工作流框架，联合决定测量方式、扫描速率与是否重校准，结合显式科学奖励、动作成本、仪器观测模型和预实验知识迁移，并在真实电子能量损失谱数据上比较不同采集策略与替代模型，附独立误差审计。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按成本决定「获取何种证据、以何精度、何时停止或重校准」的序列决策，以及关于模型不确定性何时不是可靠学习信号的负面结论，可能为 LVR 的 LOOK/STOP 收益成本权衡与视觉证据筛选提供概念类比，可供核查。
